rationale: Targeted check: all 4 prior blocking findings (CR-001..CR-004) are resolved on current source at HEAD (Optional replaced by unions, generics parameterized, rollback link_contracts=False asserted, entry id seed extended and tested); no new findings discovered this round, 0 deferred re-checked. Tests were not run here; green execution is Stage 7 evidence.

findings.title: Use X | None unions in new models
findings.problem: code-quality.md requires X | None unions over typing.Optional[X] in new code. The new ValidateNewWorkflowRequest (workflow_models.py) and ContractMeta plus the new config_path/outcome fields (validation/models.py) use Optional[...].
findings.impact: A documented code-quality standard is broken in newly added code, so the change is not conformant with the project's blocking quality bar.
findings.recommendation: Write the new annotations as str | None, WorkflowMode | None and list[...] | None instead of Optional[...].
findings.check_notes: ValidateNewWorkflowRequest fields and ContractMeta/config_path/outcome now use X | None unions; remaining Optional lines are pre-existing fields.

fix.change: ValidateNewWorkflowRequest, ContractMeta.label, config_path, outcome and meta now use X | None unions

findings.title: Parameterize bare dict/list annotations
findings.problem: code-quality.md says to prefer parameterized generics over bare list/dict annotations in new code. New modules use request_dump: dict, coverage: dict | None, items: list | None (save_validation.py:52,64,100,125,217) and ContractIssues errors/warnings: list[dict], coverage: dict, tuple[dict, str] (contract_issues.py:70-72,104).
findings.impact: A documented code-quality standard is broken in newly added modules, so the change is not conformant.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize the generics, for example dict[str, Any], dict[str, object], list[dict[str, Any]] and tuple[dict[str, Any], str].
findings.check_notes: Annotations parameterized to dict[str, Any] / list[dict[str, Any]] / tuple[dict[str, Any], str] in save_validation.py and contract_issues.py; no bare dict/list annotations remain.

fix.change: Parameterized bare dict/list annotations in save_validation.py and contract_issues.py (dict[str, Any], list[dict[str, Any]], tuple[dict[str, Any], str])

findings.title: Assert rollback never links contracts
findings.problem: _validate_restored_workflow passes link_contracts=False to keep rollback out of contract linking, but no test asserts it at the rollback entry point. test_workflow_version_service.py only asserts the validator mock was called; the only no-link test calls save_validation.validate directly.
findings.impact: If link_contracts=False is removed or defaulted to None, rollback on a flag-on platform starts linking and could reject a restore of an older version with a blocking contract record; no test would fail.
findings.recommendation: In tests/codemie/service/test_workflow_version_service.py, run rollback_to_version with WORKFLOW_CONTRACT_LINKING_ENABLED patched True and a wrapped validate_workflow_with_report, then assert the linked argument is False (or link_workflow_contracts is not called).
findings.check_notes: test_rollback_never_links_contracts_even_when_the_platform_flag_is_on runs rollback with the flag patched True and asserts the linked arg (args[3]) is False; matches validate_workflow_with_report call signature.

fix.change: Added rollback test with the contract flag on asserting validate_workflow_with_report receives link_contracts False

findings.title: Entry id seed can collide within one response
findings.problem: _issue_id seeds uuid5 on state|path|kind|message only. Two records identical on those but differing by field or provenance producers (e.g. strict consumer-form findings) get the same id in one response.
findings.impact: Clients keying cards or parity checks on id collapse or mis-attribute issues. Reachability was unconfirmed: the seed follows the spec and message templates may usually differ, so this is capped at major.
findings.recommendation: Add the record field and provenance producers to the seed, e.g. f"{consumer_state_id}|{path}|{kind}|{message}|{field}|{provenance.producers}", and add a test with two records differing only by producer.
findings.check_notes: _issue_id seed now includes record.field and provenance producers; test covers records differing only by field or producer.

fix.change: _issue_id seed now includes record.field and provenance producers (tolerates missing provenance)
